Re-anchored on anchor.jacob_birth (offset 76 y 10 m, margin 1 y) at the reviewer's request. Gen 27 puts Jacob's flight at about 63 (the corpus date 1943 BCE against anchor.jacob_birth 2006 BCE), so this leaves an unnarrated gap of about 14 years after Bethel (28:22) before the arrival. It is forced by the fixed ends: Jacob was 130 before Pharaoh (47:9), Joseph 30 at 41:46 plus 7 plenty and 2 famine years (45:6) gives Joseph born when Jacob was 91; Joseph was born as the 14 years of service ended (30:25; 31:41). Fourteen years back is Jacob 77 on arrival; Rashi on 29:21 has Jacob 84 at the request for Rachel, which agrees (77 plus one month plus seven years). The text narrates nothing of those years, and the Bethel-to-Haran journey is still 29 days on foot per urim travel. 'The land of the sons of the east' is taken as the region of Haran; 29:4 confirms the shepherds are from Haran.

agent_notes: Hebrew days run sunset to sunset, so the feast of 29:22 and 'the evening' of 29:23 are counted as the same civil day: the feast is placed at midday of the day of the wedding (the hour is my estimate), the night starts at EREV, and the discovery is the next BOKER. Pseudo-Jonathan's expansion that the town conspired with Laban is not used.

'Fulfil her week' (29:27) is read, with Rashi, Rashbam, Ibn Ezra, Ramban and Pseudo-Jonathan, as the seven days of Leah's wedding feast. Rachel is given at the end of that week, so seven days after Leah's wedding night at sunset. Ramban reports the other reading (a week of years, as Onkelos is sometimes taken). The text says Jacob served the further seven years after receiving Rachel (29:30), and I follow that.

The births of Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah carry no time words. They are spaced at about 11 months, with margins of 3 months, so that Judah is born in about the fourth year of the second seven and the births of Genesis 30 (Dan to Joseph) still fit before the 14th year. The tier is REGNAL_YEAR because the scene falls inside the stated seven-year periods; the spacing is an estimate.

The first seven years run from the wage agreement. Counting 14 years of service to Joseph's birth at the end of the second seven (30:25-26; 31:41 gives 20 years in all), Joseph's birth lands in Jacob's 91st year, which agrees with anchor.joseph_birth (Jacob 91). Rashi on 29:21 says Jacob was 84 when he asked for Rachel, so that tradition has him 77 on arrival and 91 at Joseph's birth, which fits the same chain.
